## Proof

**Claim.** Let \(F:\mathcal{J}\to\mathcal{C}\) be a functor and \(N\) an object of \(\mathcal{C}\). Whenever the colimit \(\varinjlim F\) exists in \(\mathcal{C}\), there is a natural isomorphism of sets

\[
\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}\!\bigl(\varinjlim F,\; N\bigr)\;\cong\;\varprojlim_{X\in\mathcal{J}}\,\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}\!\bigl(F(X),\; N\bigr),
\]

where the limit on the right is taken in \(\mathbf{Set}\) over the functor

\[
\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(-),\,N):\mathcal{J}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set},\qquad X\;\mapsto\;\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N).
\]

In words: **the covariant hom-functor \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,N)\) carries colimits in \(\mathcal{C}\) to limits in \(\mathbf{Set}\).** This is the statement that \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,N)\) is **limit-preserving** (equivalently, sends colimits to limits), i.e. it is a **right adjoint** in each variable.

---

### Setup

Let \((L,\{\iota_X:L\to F(X)\}_{X\in\mathcal{J}})\) be a colimit cocone of \(F\), so \(L=\varinjlim F\). For every morphism \(\alpha:X\to Y\) in \(\mathcal{J}\) we have the compatibility \(F(\alpha)\circ\iota_X=\iota_Y\)... wait — for a **co**cone the arrows go \(F(X)\to L\); let me fix the direction. A colimit cocone consists of maps \(\iota_X:F(X)\to L\) with \(\iota_Y\circ F(\alpha)=\iota_X\) for every \(\alpha:X\to Y\) in \(\mathcal{J}\).

Applying \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,N)\) (contravariant in its first argument) to each \(\iota_X\) gives a map

\[
\iota_X^{*}:\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(L,N)\longrightarrow\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N),\qquad f\mapsto f\circ\iota_X.
\]

The cocone compatibility \(\iota_Y\circ F(\alpha)=\iota_X\) translates, after applying \((-)^{*}\), into

\[
F(\alpha)^{*}\circ\iota_Y^{*}=\iota_X^{*},
\]

i.e. the family \(\{\iota_X^{*}\}_{X}\) is a **cone** over the diagram \(X\mapsto\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N)\) (a functor \(\mathcal{J}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}\)). By the universal property of the limit, this cone factors uniquely through a map

\[
\Phi:\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(L,N)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{X}\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N),
\]

defined by \(\Phi(f)=(f\circ\iota_X)_{X\in\mathcal{J}}\).

---

### \(\Phi\) is bijective

**Injectivity.** Suppose \(\Phi(f)=\Phi(g)\), i.e. \(f\circ\iota_X=g\circ\iota_X\) for all \(X\). Then \(f\) and \(g\) agree on every leg of the colimit cocone. By the universal property of the colimit, two maps out of \(L\) that agree on the entire cocone are equal: \(f=g\).

**Surjectivity.** Let \((h_X\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N))_{X\in\mathcal{J}}\) be an element of the limit, i.e. a compatible family: for every \(\alpha:X\to Y\) in \(\mathcal{J}\),

\[
h_Y\circ F(\alpha)=h_X.
\]

This compatibility is exactly the condition that the family \(\{h_X:F(X)\to N\}\) is a **cocone** over \(F\) with vertex \(N\). By the universal property of the colimit \(L=\varinjlim F\), there exists a unique map \(h:L\to N\) with \(h\circ\iota_X=h_X\) for all \(X\). Then \(\Phi(h)=(h_X)_{X}\), so \((h_X)\) is in the image of \(\Phi\).

Hence \(\Phi\) is a bijection.

---

### Naturality in \(N\)

For a morphism \(u:N\to N'\) in \(\mathcal{C}\), post-composition gives a commutative square

\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(L,N) & \xrightarrow{\Phi_N} & \varprojlim_{X}\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N)\\[4pt]
{\scriptstyle u\circ-}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle u\circ-}\\[4pt]
\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(L,N') & \xrightarrow{\Phi_{N'}} & \varprojlim_{X}\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(F(X),N')
\end{array}
\]

since \((u\circ h)\circ\iota_X=u\circ(h\circ\iota_X)\) componentwise. Thus \(\Phi\) is natural in \(N\).

---

### Conclusion

The relationship is the canonical natural isomorphism

\[
\boxed{\;\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}\!\bigl(\varinjlim_{\mathcal{J}} F,\; N\bigr)\;\cong\;\varprojlim_{X\in\mathcal{J}}\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}\!\bigl(F(X),\; N\bigr)\;}
\]

exhibiting the fact that the representable functor \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,N):\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}\) **sends colimits in \(\mathcal{C}\) to limits in \(\mathbf{Set}\)**. This is the dual of the more familiar statement that \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(M,-)\) preserves limits, and both are instances of the general principle that **left/right adjoints preserve colimits/limits** — here \(\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal{C}}(-,N)\) being a right adjoint (its left adjoint is \(-\otimes N\) when \(\mathcal{C}\) is suitably closed) preserves limits, dually sending colimits to limits.

### PROOF COMPLETE
